messages:
Priya Nair: Quick threadwe need a crisp contract for model pinning + fallback across hosted/dedicated/private. Current blur causes mismatched tokenization and hallucination regressions when requests cross modes.

Daniel Kim: +1. Observed a customer hit with different bytepair vocab between private runtime and hosted variant. We should define compatibility tiers, not just names.

Omar Ruiz: Proposed tiers: 'ABI-compatible' (same weights + tokenizer + kv-layout), 'API-compatible' (same API but different quantization/latency tradeoffs), 'Semantic-compatible' (best-effort semantics). Each tier implies different fallback behaviors.

Hannah Lee: Nice. For ABI-compatible we can do transparent fallback. For API-compatible, proxy should rewrite response hints (e.g., attach model_variant header) and run post-hoc regression checks. For semantic-compatible, require explicit opt-in or downgrade to a graceful error.

Priya Nair: Who owns the regression check? control plane runs canary evals, but runtime should do quick smoke checks (tokenization parity, sample perplexity delta) to avoid obvious breakages in request path.

Daniel Kim: Smoke checks must be cheap. Suggest: 1) tokenization checksum (first N tokens), 2) anchor prompt set (5-10 short prompts) run in <50ms path using cached warm model slices. If check fails -> proxy switches to fallback policy.

Omar Ruiz: What fallback policy? soft-fallback (serve hosted variant with banner + telemetry) vs hard-fallback (reject and route to user-owned private lane). Soft-fallback can break SLAs if semantic drift is large.

Hannah Lee: Add a third option: 'degraded-mode' where we serve cached completions (from KV cache) while we revalidate a model variant. That helps low-throughput mission-critical customers.

Priya Nair: We also need a manifest field for model compatibility metadata: model_id, shard_layout, tokenizer_kid, quant_profile, semantic_checksum. Control plane publishes to proxies and private agents.

Daniel Kim: Key rotation/manifest propagation issue: if private is pinned to an old tokenizer kid and hosted publishes new kid, proxies must have strict version resolution. Suggest manifest includes supported_kids list and 'preferred' flag.

Omar Ruiz: TTLs: manifest updates should be staged. Proxies cache manifest for M seconds (configurable). On mismatch, proxy triggers an async revalidation against control plane and may sidecar-call if private exists.

Hannah Lee: Observability: emit events: manifest_mismatch, smoke_check_fail, fallback_triggered, degraded_cache_hit. Make them high-cardinality with model_id and tenant.

Priya Nair: Security/PII note: regression prompts used in smoke checks must be synthetic or customer-provided testset hashed. Never run live customer prompts for parity checks.

Daniel Kim: Operational playbook: 1) When deploying a new variant, tag compatibility tier and run cross-mode evals, 2) stage manifest to 5% proxies, 3) watch smoke_check_fail rate and degraded_cache_hit, 4) roll forward/rollback.

Omar Ruiz: Edge-case: streaming responses and incremental KV cache differences. We should define a stream resumption protocol: include model_variant and resume_token; if model changes mid-stream, fail with 409-stream-variant and offer client-driven retry.

Hannah Lee: Client SDKs need helpers: on 409-stream-variant, they can automatically re-open with resume_token and model_pref. Document recommended retry windows and exponential backoff.

Priya Nair: Billing/Quota implications: if we reroute to hosted for a private-request, charge should follow the execution mode. Add audit header to correlate billing records.

Daniel Kim: Migration path for customers: provide a 'compatibility shadow' mode where private traffic is mirrored to candidate hosted variant for 24-72 hours to gather semantic checks before flip.

Omar Ruiz: Implementation sketch: manifest + compatibility tier, smoke-check lib in proxy runtime (opt-in per-tenant), fallback queue and degraded-cache layer, stream-resume semantics, and canary rollout plan.

Hannah Lee: I'll assemble a minimal RFC with manifest schema + smoke-check pseudocode + sample headers (x-redwood-model-variant, x-redwood-smoke-status, x-redwood-fallback-reason) and a migration checklist.

SRE-bot: Canary scheduled: model-variant-manifest-rollout at 03:00 UTC. Watch manifest_mismatch_rate, smoke_check_fail_rate, and degraded_cache_hit_pct.

Priya Nair: Thanks all. Priorities: manifest schema first, then smoke-check lib, then stream-resume. Ping me when the RFC is ready for review. :white_check_mark:
